wiki.extract: Milford Sound is a fiord in the south west of New Zealand's South Island within Fiordland National Park, Piopiotahi Marine Reserve, and the Te Wahipounamu World Heritage site. It has been judged the world's top travel destination in an international survey and is acclaimed as New Zealand's most famous tourist destination. Rudyard Kipling called it the eighth Wonder of the World. The fiord is most commonly accessed via road by tour coach, with the road terminating at a small village also called Milford Sound.

The Sky Tower is a telecommunications and observation tower in Auckland, New Zealand. Located at the corner of Victoria and Federal Streets within the city's CBD, it is 328 metres (1,076 ft) tall, as measured from ground level to the top of the mast, making it the second-tallest freestanding structure in the Southern Hemisphere, surpassed only by the Autograph Tower in Jakarta, Indonesia, and the 28th tallest tower in the world. Since its completion in 1997, the Sky Tower has become an iconic landmark in Auckland's skyline, due to its height and design. It was the tallest freestanding structure in the Southern Hemisphere from 1996 to 2022.

Tongariro National Park, located in the central North Island, is the oldest national park in New Zealand and the sixth national park established in the world. It has been recognised by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site for its mixed cultural and natural values.

Waitomo, officially Waitomo Caves, is a rural community in the King Country region of New Zealand's North Island. There are several solutional cave systems in the area around the village, which are popular tourist attractions. Restaurants and accommodation are centred in the village to serve visiting tourists.

The Hobbiton Movie Set is a significant location used for The Lord of the Rings film trilogy and The Hobbit film trilogy, serving as a stand-in for the town of Hobbiton in the Shire in both trilogies. It is situated on a family-run farm about 8 kilometres (5.0 mi) west of Hinuera and 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) southwest of Matamata, in Waikato, New Zealand, and is now a Tolkien tourism destination, offering a guided tour of the set.

wiki.extract: Waitangi Day, the national day of New Zealand, marks the anniversary of the initial signing of the Treaty of Waitangi on 6 February 1840. The Treaty of Waitangi was an agreement towards British sovereignty by representatives of the Crown and indigenous Māori chiefs, and so is regarded by many as the founding document of the nation.
In Māori culture, Matariki is the Pleiades star cluster and a celebration of its first rising in late June or early July. The rising marks the beginning of the new year in the Māori lunar calendar.

The Pasifika Festival is a festival celebrating Pasifika New Zealanders and their pan-cultural identity, held annually in Western Springs Reserve, Auckland. Celebrated since 1993, it is the largest festival of its type in the world and attracts over 200,000 visitors every year.

The New Zealand International Film Festival (NZIFF) (Māori: Whānau Mārama) is a film festival held annually across New Zealand. The festival is operated by the New Zealand Film Festival Trust. It programmes international and New Zealand films.

World of WearableArt (WOW) is an international design competition with a corresponding event each year. It attracts entries from more than 40 countries each year. The competition features wearable art entries. Around 60,000 people attend the event in Wellington, New Zealand.

food_writeup: New Zealand cuisine reflects its diverse cultural heritage with a focus on fresh seafood, lamb, and dairy products. Traditional Mnori foods like hangi (earth-cooked meals) coexist with modern fusion dishes.
brief_history: New Zealand was first settled by Polynesian Mnori around 1300 AD. European exploration began in the 17th century, with British colonization formalized by the Treaty of Waitangi in 1840. It evolved into a self-governing dominion and is now a constitutional monarchy with a strong democratic tradition.
current_conflicts: New Zealand currently has no significant internal or external conflicts; it maintains a peaceful foreign policy and active participation in international peacekeeping.

commentary.inflation_management: The RBNZ pioneered formal inflation targeting in 1990 and mostly kept CPI in its 1-3% band through 2020, with the series low of 0.3% in 2015 and a 2008 peak of 4%. The post-COVID surge broke the pattern: 3.9% in 2021, a series high of 7.2% in 2022 and 5.7% in 2023, driven by housing, supply chains and a tight labour market. The RBNZ was among the first central banks to tighten, lifting the official cash rate from 0.25% to 5.5% between late 2021 and 2023 - a deliberately demand-destroying move that pushed the economy into a shallow recession. It worked: inflation fell to 2.9% in 2024 and a projected 2.8% in 2025, back at the top of the target band. The episode reinforced the RBNZ's hawkish credibility at real output cost.
commentary.debt_management: Gross debt rose from 18.4% of GDP in 2006 to 35.7% by 2012, driven by the GFC and the costly Canterbury earthquake rebuild, then fell steadily to 28.1% by 2018 under fiscal consolidation. COVID-era spending pushed it to 43.2% in 2020, and unlike Australia it has kept climbing every year since, reaching a series high of 54.7% in the 2025 projection as post-COVID deficits persisted through weak growth. The level remains low by advanced-economy standards, is NZD-denominated, and has not threatened the sovereign rating; the concern is the trajectory, with deficits now structural rather than cyclical.

key_events.event: Global financial crisis: recession and a sharp rise in debt from 19% to 24.3% of GDP.
February Christchurch earthquake devastated the city and drove a multi-year, debt-funded rebuild.
Jacinda Ardern's Labour-led government took office after the September election, shifting fiscal and housing policy.
March Christchurch mosque attacks - the country's worst mass shooting, prompting rapid gun-law reform.
COVID-19 elimination strategy kept cases near zero but closed borders to tourism and migration.
Aggressive RBNZ tightening to 5.5% tamed 7.2% inflation but pushed the economy into recession.
October election returned a National-led government under Christopher Luxon, pivoting to fiscal restraint.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: Inflation is back near target and rate cuts should support a cyclical recovery, but trend growth is held back by weak productivity, housing unaffordability and infrastructure deficits. Debt is likely to stabilize rather than fall quickly unless fiscal consolidation bites. Key uncertainties are dairy and tourism demand from China, migration policy swings, and whether the economy can lift productivity without reigniting house-price inflation. The institutional framework - independent RBNZ, transparent fiscal rules - remains the anchor.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
